newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill reporter, wound politician in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill reporter, wound politician in Karachi.

text.p: Gunmen attacked an ethnic leader in Karachi early on Wednesday, wounding him and killing a visiting journalist, police said.

They said the gunmen opened fire on Kamran Rizvi, a leader of the breakaway Haqiqi faction of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM), as he left his house to see off his friend Manzar Imkani, a senior sub-editor at the Urdu-language Jang newspaper.
Imkani, 49, died instantly while Rizvi, 35, was seriously wounded. Neighbours took him to hospital.
A Haqiqi spokesman accused the mainstream MQM of carrying out the attack. MQM officials denied responsibility.
On Tuesday a partial strike closed shops and businesses in southern parts of Karachi as residents mourned five MQM activists killed in a drive-by shooting the night before.
MQM blamed Haqiqi for the killings. Haqiqi denied the charge.
Violence has risen in the volatile port city in recent weeks amid tension between the MQM, now part of a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, and Haqiqi.
More than 80 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian violence in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
